claim: On a PCIe system with no peer-to-peer access, every inter-GPU byte is staged through host memory and therefore crosses the PCIe bus twice, once on the sender's write to a pinned host buffer and once on the receiver's read back.
stance_target: the repo's premise that a no-P2P fabric makes all collectives host-staged and roughly halves effective bandwidth
scope_conditions: NVIDIA consumer GPUs (RTX 40/50 series) with PCIe P2P disabled by the driver; intra-node communication
quoted_support: As shown in Figure 4b, the sender writes the payload to a pinned host buffer, and the receiver reads it back, so every byte traverses PCIe bus twice.

claim: NCCL's ring All-Gather transfers 2(N-1)S bytes per GPU on a host-staged fabric, whereas a single-step host broadcast transfers N*S, a ratio of 2(N-1)/N that equals 1.6x at five GPUs.
stance_target: the claim that NCCL's default ring algorithm is structurally wasteful without P2P, and that the penalty grows with GPU count
scope_conditions: N GPUs in one node, per-GPU shard size S, no P2P so every hop is a host round trip
quoted_support: The ring transfers 2(N-1)S bytes per GPU, one upload and one download at each of its N-1 sequential steps... ThunderEP transfers N*S bytes per GPU... The ratio of PCIe transfer volume between the two is 2(N-1)/N, which equals one at N=2 and grows toward two as the node fills.

claim: PCIe bandwidth available to each GPU degrades as more GPUs communicate concurrently: a single RTX 5090 reaches 56.5 GB/s alone on PCIe Gen5 x16, but two GPUs under the same host bridge communicating at once fall to 35.5 GB/s each.
stance_target: the claim that per-GPU collective bandwidth on a shared PCIe hierarchy is well below the nominal link rate and shrinks with participant count
scope_conditions: 6x RTX 5090, three PCIe host bridges with two GPUs each, single NUMA node, PCIe 5.0 x16
quoted_support: Measurements in our PCIe-based RTX 5090 system (Table 1), a GPU communicating alone reaches 56.5 GB/s on PCIe Gen5, close to its theoretical bandwidth of 64 GB/s. When a second GPU under the same PCIe host bridge communicates concurrently, the bandwidth of each GPU falls to 35.5 GB/s.

claim: A single-step host-broadcast EP collective plus DMA-engine transfers and per-sender completion flags beats NCCL by 2.00x on MoE dispatch and 1.53x on combine on PCIe consumer GPUs without P2P.
stance_target: the claim that host-staged EP communication can be substantially optimized, so EP is degraded rather than impossible on a no-P2P fabric
scope_conditions: 6x RTX 4090 and 6x RTX 5090, no GPUDirect P2P between any pair, Qwen3-30B-A3B / GPT-OSS-20B / GPT-OSS-120B, vLLM 0.27.1 baseline, NCCL 2.30.7
quoted_support: Across two PCIe systems equipped with two recent generations of consumer GPUs, ThunderEP improves dispatch and combine communication performance over NCCL by 2.00x and 1.53x, respectively.

claim: End-to-end MoE inference gains from fixing host-staged EP communication are large: up to 1.66x prefill speedup and up to 1.26x decode throughput over vLLM, with exposed MoE communication latency cut 64.4% in prefill and 50.1% in decode.
stance_target: the claim that communication, not compute, is the binding constraint for MoE on a PCIe consumer-GPU node
scope_conditions: RTX 5090 system, batch 24, prompt lengths 256-4K for prefill, 4K prompt and batch 6-96 for decode
quoted_support: Together, ThunderEP reduces the exposed MoE communication latency by 64.4% and the total Transformer layer latency by 38.9%... During decode, compared with vLLM, ThunderEP reduces the exposed MoE communication latency by 50.1%, lowering the Transformer layer latency by 15.2%.

claim: All existing MoE-specialized EP communication libraries (DeepEP, pplx-kernels, NCCL EP, UCCL-EP, NIXL) assume NVLink, GPUDirect P2P or RDMA and cannot operate on a consumer-GPU node with P2P disabled.
stance_target: the repo's claim that expert parallelism is effectively ruled out on the CMP 170HX fabric, because the optimized EP stacks do not run there
scope_conditions: as of 2026; consumer GPUs lacking NVLink and with PCIe P2P disabled by the driver
quoted_support: Their designs, however, assume that GPUs can directly access one another through NVLink, GPUDirect Peer-to-Peer (P2P) or RDMA... Consequently, existing EP communication libraries cannot operate on these systems.

claim: When top-k exceeds the expert-parallel size, an All-Gather plus Reduce-Scatter formulation outperforms two All-to-All collectives and is the default EP backend in Megatron-Core and vLLM.
stance_target: which collective shape an EP experiment on a slow fabric should implement
scope_conditions: fine-grained MoE where each token reaches many destination GPUs; top-k >= number of EP ranks
quoted_support: A recent study similarly reports that All-Gather followed by Reduce-Scatter outperforms two All-to-All collectives when top-k exceeds the number of GPUs. Several state-of-the-art MoE systems, including Megatron-Core and vLLM, therefore adopt an implementation of All-Gather and Reduce-Scatter as their default EP communication backend.

claim: Routing-aware (data-dependent) All-to-All is not worth implementing on a host-staged consumer-GPU fabric: the CPU must fetch routing metadata before issuing each DMA transfer, and the resulting CPU-GPU synchronization plus many small requests offset the PCIe traffic saved.
stance_target: the idea that trimming EP traffic to only the routed tokens rescues EP on a no-P2P fabric
scope_conditions: DMA transfers issued through host APIs while routing decisions are generated on the GPU
quoted_support: The CPU must therefore retrieve the routing metadata before issuing transfers at every MoE layer, introducing CPU-GPU synchronization and numerous small DMA requests. In our measurements, these overheads offset the reduction in PCIe traffic.

claim: On these PCIe systems the aggregate PCIe bandwidth exceeds available host DRAM bandwidth, so CPU-side reduction of combine traffic costs more time than the PCIe traffic it saves.
stance_target: the claim that host memory itself, not just the link, becomes a bottleneck once several GPUs stream through it concurrently
scope_conditions: 6-GPU PCIe nodes with DDR5-4800 host memory
quoted_support: On our systems, the aggregate PCIe bandwidth exceeds the available host DRAM bandwidth, leaving little bandwidth for CPU reduction. The resulting CPU reduction overhead exceeds the time saved by reducing PCIe traffic.
numbers: aggregate PCIe BW > host DRAM BW

claim: Expert parallelism places two All-to-All collectives (dispatch and combine) on the critical path of every MoE layer, so EP communication cost scales with the number of MoE layers, not with model size alone.
stance_target: the repo's estimate that EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer and therefore multiplies communication by layer count
scope_conditions: EP with DP-replicated attention; modern fine-grained MoE
quoted_support: As shown in Figure 1b, MoE on multiple devices with EP, occurs with two All-to-All collective communications in a single forward pass. The expert computation is thus enclosed by communication on both sides.

claim: NCCL's communication kernels occupy GPU SMs and therefore contend with expert GEMMs when overlapped; DMA-engine transfers avoid this contention but cannot perform data-dependent gather/scatter.
stance_target: the claim that SM-resident collectives steal compute from training/inference on a bandwidth-starved node
scope_conditions: NCCL collective kernels vs DMA copy engines on consumer GPUs
quoted_support: NCCL performs its collective operations using kernels that occupy the GPU SMs. When communication overlaps with expert computation, the two operations compete for the same SM resources... DMA engines avoid this contention by moving data without occupying the SMs, but each transfer incurs a fixed issue overhead and can access only contiguous or fixed stride regions.

claim: Ablation on Qwen3-30B-A3B at 4K input shows prefill TTFT falling from 2115.9 ms (vLLM baseline) to 1436.4 ms with the full ThunderEP design, a 1.47x prefill speedup, while decode TPOT falls from 10.10 ms to 8.78 ms (1.15x).
stance_target: how much of the EP overhead is algorithmic (ring relays) versus transfer-mechanism (SM kernels, flag polling)
quoted_support: Baseline (vLLM) 2115.9 TTFT (ms) 10.10 TPOT (ms) 1.00x 1.00x; + Algorithm and synchronization 1844.7 8.77 1.15x 1.15x; + DMA transfer 1722.8 8.78 1.23x 1.15x; + DMA-based overlap 1436.4 8.78 1.47x 1.15x
